To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the isolation of allophycobyanin B (APB), the allophycocoyanin‐containing core complex of hemidiscoidal cyanobacterial phycobilisosomes, was performed for the first time and that a model of this complex was constructed.
the isolation and characterization of allophycocyani B from the phycobilosomes of Rhodella (Glaucosphaera) violacea resulted in a model of hemidiscoidal core complexes.
the allophycocayanin B complex is composed of two α∗Apα‐dimers (α∗AP) which are associated with one β∗AP and two βAP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of allophycocyainin B from the hemidiscoildal phycobilisoms of Rhodella violacea.
the isolation of the allophycocayanin B from the hemidicsoidal phycobiliosomes of the red alga Rhodella violace.
the isolation of allophycocyamin B from Rhodalla violacea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hemidiscoid of Rhodella is composed of a core with a trimeric structure of allophycobin B (α∗ ApαAPβ2 APβ ∗AP) with the linker polypeptides (Lc12.5 and LC13.5APb).
the allophycocianin B is the central component of the core complex of the rhodophycean phycobilisomal system.
allophycocayan B is the core complex of the hemidiscoids of Rhodella phycobilisosomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phycobiliprotein complexes AP and APB are the constituents of the core of hemidiscoidal rhodophytic phycobilisomers.
the phycobiliproteins from Rhodella are not identical to those of Porphyridium.
the allophycocayanin B of Rhodella contains two different α‐polypeptides (αAp, αB) which are linked by the linker polypeptide Lc 13,5APB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the allophycocayanin B complex is a trimeric structure, which contains two allophycocanin B monomers, one allophycocanylin A monomer, and two β‐subunits.
the linker polypeptide Lc 13,5APB is the only linker polypeptide that is able to bind to both α‐ and β‐allophycocyanins.
the allophycocayanin core of the hemidiscoid is composed of two allophycocanin complexes, AP and APB.
